findings.text: follow-on: _names_a_figure_record re-derives the review store's rubric-in-filename convention (f"{FIGURE_REVIEW_RUBRIC}." in path.name) that review.review_path (reckon/crew/review.py:2098) is the sole owner of, and _figure_review_files (promotion_checks.py:578) re-derives the candidate-path enumeration (staging glob plus committed run directory) that review.stored_record (reckon/crew/review.py:3566-3588) owns. Neither extends its owner: a change to the store's figure-file naming or layout would silently stop this guard recognising its own subject and it would fail open in exactly the class it was added to close. The read half does reuse the owner (stored_record skips unreadable files into the caller's skipped list), so this is a partial duplication rather than a from-scratch reimplementation.

follow-on: the head-arm gate log the manifest names for this delta's code (logs/gate-unreadable-figure.log) records "# revision: b91979eb6" over an uncommitted working tree, not the committed revisions febf84aed or bafe7eb91, so a reader resolving the manifest's gate to the recorded head sha finds no log naming it. I re-ran the process's own suite in the run's worktree at bafe7eb91 and confirmed 6 passed, so the code is sound; the gap is in the recorded provenance of the head arm, not in the behaviour.

follow-on: the coordinator's population head arm (coordinator-population-head.log, 7 failed / 844 passed at b91979eb6) adds test_a_launch_that_wrote_a_turn_is_not_a_launch_failure against the base arm (coordinator-population-base.log, 6 failed / 841 passed at d839407e). The file is not touched by this node and the failure is unrelated to the figure guard, so it reads as flaky or environmental, but it is the one added failure id the two arms report and is recorded so a reader can attribute or retire it.
